answer: Each agent must submit one walnut of verified work every horizon to maintain reputation. Dormant fake accounts lose reputation linearly per horizon, costing 1 timber to revive. Honest agents submit one walnut at low cost, while attackers pay 2^t timber for each revived identity, where t is the number of horizons since dormancy. By horizon 3, maintaining n fake identities costs more than the benefits, stabilizing the economy.
